ForecastEnvelope.description:
The top-level response shape named in docs/CANONICAL_ROADMAP.md's
"Required API surface" section. `conditions`, `tides`, `hourly_outlook`,
and `recommendations` are opaque here on purpose — see module docstring.
ForecastEnvelope.title: ForecastEnvelope

ForecastLayout.description:
How a user has arranged the forecast page's tabbed sections
(apps/web's ForecastTabs). `tabs` maps a tab key to the section ids
placed there, in order -- a section can be moved to another tab, and
any section not listed stays in its default tab, after the listed
ones. `hidden` lists sections the user hid. Ids are opaque short
slugs owned by apps/web; unknown ones are simply ignored there.
ForecastLayout.title: ForecastLayout

A resolved location. Coordinates are rounded before storage/transit
per docs/CANONICAL_ROADMAP.md's data-minimization requirement — rounding
itself happens at resolution time (sprint 18/19), not here.

lat.description: Rounded, not precise — see module docstring.
lat.title: Lat

lng.description: Rounded, not precise — see module docstring.
lng.title: Lng

LocationResolveRequest.description:
Exactly one of `location_id`, or both `lat` and `lng`, must be

LocationResolveRequest.title: LocationResolveRequest

PreferencesOut.description:
Response shape. Always returns a full object, even for a user with
no row yet (sprint 36's endpoint creates one with these same
defaults on first read) -- a `404` for "no preferences set yet" would
make every new user's first `GET` an error case for no real reason.
PreferencesOut.title: PreferencesOut

PreferencesUpdate.description:
`PATCH` body -- every field optional and omitted fields are left
unchanged (a real partial update, not a `PUT`-style full replace).
`None` is a meaningful, distinct value from "omitted": it clears a
previously-set threshold/style/default location, which is why every
field below is `T | None` rather than plain `T` with an implicit
can't-unset gap. `exclude_unset=True` at the call site is what
reads that distinction back out of the request body.
PreferencesUpdate.title: PreferencesUpdate

Regulation.description:
Recreational limits for one species in one state, from the legacy
snapshot (provisional -- always shown with its age and official link).
Regulation.title: Regulation

ResolvedLocation.description:
A forecast-ready location — either a curated spot as-is, or an
assembled dynamic point. `is_dynamic=False` means every field came
directly from `CuratedLocation`; `is_dynamic=True` means station IDs
were resolved from live catalogs and the coarse regional fields were
inherited from the nearest curated neighbor (see
`resolve_dynamic_location`).

`anchor_miles` is `None` for a curated location — it *is* the named
spot, so there's no meaningful "distance to the nearest real
station" to report — and for a dynamic point where no anchor
(curated neighbor, CO-OPS station, or NDBC buoy) was found at all.
Otherwise it's `resolve_dynamic_location`'s nearest-anchor distance,
added so a later confidence assessment (`app.domain.confidence`) has
real distance data to work with instead of none at all.
ResolvedLocation.title: ResolvedLocation

SavedLocationOut.description:
`location_id`'s display fields (`name`/`state`/`lat`/`lng`) are
resolved fresh at read time via the same `resolve_location_id` every
forecast lookup uses, not stored and left to go stale -- a curated
location's own name/state never changes, but resolving live keeps
this one code path instead of two ways to know a location's name.
SavedLocationOut.title: SavedLocationOut
